notes: EBIT is proxied as 'Operating income' (operating income / operating results), using the consolidated statement of earnings. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

D&A is taken from the consolidated statement line 'Depreciation and amortization' (income statement line item). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

Capex is taken from cash flow line 'Purchase of property and equipment' and converted from 'in thousands' to full dollars. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

NWC is calculated as (Total current assets - cash and cash equivalents) - Total current liabilities. This includes contract liabilities/deferred contract costs and taxes payable as they appear in the current assets/liabilities totals; this may differ from alternative NWC constructions that exclude deferred/contract balances. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))
WACC is assumed (not directly provided in the filings); adjust if your DCF framework derives WACC from a specific capital market methodology.

NOL balance and utilization were not found in the accessible extracted portions of the FY2025 10-K; set to null. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Material improvement in freight demand/volumes and/or pricing conditions across air and ocean lanes supporting revenue growth continuation.
Sustained operating discipline enabling EBIT margin to hold in the base-case band despite cyclical trade conditions.
Potential working-capital normalization improving free-cash-flow conversion in periods following elevated deferred/contract-related balances.
company_overview: Expeditors is a global logistics services provider with revenues generated across airfreight services, ocean freight/ocean services, and customs brokerage and other services. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

The business model emphasizes shipment consolidation and customer services supporting international transportation and trade compliance. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))
FY2025 results: total revenues of 11069009000 and operating income (EBIT proxy) of 1052546000. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))
current_context: Q4 2025 earnings release (Feb 24, 2026): full-year 2025 operating income of 1052546000 and revenues of 11069009000. ([investor.expeditors.com](https://investor.expeditors.com/~/media/Files/E/Expeditors-IR-V2/press-release/2026/EXPDQ41.PDF))

2025 cash generation and shareholder returns noted by management in the annual report (cash from operations up; total returned to shareholders highlighted). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes mid-single-digit revenue growth from 2025 with EBIT margin stabilizing near the recent ~9.5%-9.8% range (defined as operating income / total revenues). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

D&A and capex are modeled as low-single-digit percentages of sales, consistent with a service-heavy logistics platform. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

Working-capital intensity is modeled as modest and relatively stable in percentage-of-sales terms, although historical NWC shows volatility across the 2023-2025 window (modeled with a conservative constant). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))

Capital structure is modeled with near-zero year-end debt per filings; therefore valuation sensitivity is driven primarily by operating assumptions and terminal economics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Downturn in global trade (tariffs, demand shocks, or route disruptions) reducing volumes and pressuring operating income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))
Foreign exchange and tax-rate volatility impacting reported results and effective cash tax burden. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000746515/000119312526071569/expd-20251231.htm))
Competition among global logistics providers and carrier capacity/rate volatility that can affect achievable pricing and spread.
